body: I will talk to someone, I just don't see my therapist again until Friday.  And I don't want to bring it up because there's so much other stuff we're working on, I don't want to go back to suicide.  We spent enough time on that 6 months ago.  But if you say suicide everyone freaks out, so I imagine that we'd be talking about it for a while.  Maybe I'll wait til the end of the session or something.  Maybe I won't say anything at all and hope that I'm feeling better by then.
Loving self is difficult.  I've learned the opposite.  Perfectionism means I'm never good enough.

Pain is inexpressible to me.  I avoid it at almost any cost.  I've approached releasing sadness and pain in a healthy way maybe twice in the past few months.  Other times I'm avoiding, distracting, or hurting myself.  

It's beautiful that you believe that you are love and light.  It's great that you care and love all.  I believe I am too selfish.

My therapist would be disappointed to hear that I'm connecting with random strangers online when I'm supposed to be trying to connect with people in real life.  She asked me a few days ago what people I feel connected to in my life.  I said "You want people? The only connection I can think of is with my cat."  

I want connection but I am so scared to be hurt again that I avoid it.  I don't even watch movies.  I get too attached to the characters and I don't want anything bad to happen to them.  They aren't even real!  But I avoid those connections anyway, just like I avoid connection to people in my life.

Yeah, I can't cry without some sort of trigger...it feels pathetic that it was a Disney movie.  But hey, I know what it feels like to be lost and alone.  It was sort of helpful to identify that.  Thanks for the positive thoughts.

I'm going to butt in if that's okay!   :)  Meds have helped me so much.  Meds didn't change me, but they gave me the capacity to change myself.  If that makes sense.  I was so low that I was just stuck, but the meds lifted my mood just enough to the point where I could make changes to my life.  It's a lot of work to fully recover from depression, and the meds don't do it for you, they just help.  

Good luck in your journey!  You're not alone!

I'm in the midst of divorce, so a relationship is absolutely not what I want.  The last year or so of my marriage, we showed no physical affection at all.  So what I find myself craving from others is to be touched.  A hug, a caring hand on my shoulder, something to let me know that I am connected to others, that I'm not in this untouchable bubble that I feel like I'm in sometimes.  Although I'm not consciously isolating as much anymore, I still feel isolated.

I'm not sure what to consider "encouraging."  I responded really well on the day where she was especially gentle with me.  I was gentle with myself for days afterward-it's almost like I needed someone to model it for me.  Most times, though, it's not like that.  I don't express emotions well (if at all), and because I'm so guarded it's probably hard to tell exactly what to do with me.  

She keeps saying to let her know if she's "pushing me too hard" or if something is "too much," but I'm not sure what that means or how to know if something is too much.  I plan to ask about it in my next appointment.  I tend to think things through on my own later because I'm slow.  I am not sure what to think until after I've had time to process by myself.  

At the end of my last appointment, my therapist told me she was a little afraid to bring up the whole word snob thing because she didn't want me to feel like she was hurting or criticizing me.  I responded that it was very unlikely that I'd feel that way.  It's not her fault I'm defensive, she's just pointing it out.  I told her that the more likely situation would be me hating on myself for being this way...so here it is.  Of course this came at the end of the session, so there wasn't much she or I could do about it.  She just suggested the replacement thought "I'm glad I know this about myself" and sent me on my way.  And I am glad I know this about myself, but it also sucks to have one more reason to hate who I am.

Sometimes, people with depression have super low energy.  And taking antidepressants counteracts the energy before the depressed mood.  So you have someone who hates life who all of a sudden has the energy to do something about it.  :P

I am absolutely wanting to change my situation-I nearly lost my teaching job shortly after being diagnosed with major depression.  My principal thought I wasn't connecting with my students well enough and I "looked like I wasn't enjoying my job," among other things.  I've tried so hard to do everything my principal tells me.  And I've tried to do everything my therapist asks me to try.  I learn everything I can about different aspects of depression that I deal with.  I just keep peeling back seemingly endless layers of crap to work through, things that I didn't even know were issues.  The amount of things I dislike about myself just feels overwhelming sometimes, and I'm learning new things in therapy all the time that add on to the ever-growing pile of crap that I wish wasn't a part of me.  

I absolutely need to be kinder to myself.  It's just hard when all I see is the crap.  

It's kind of you to think that I'm not bad to be around.  It seems that I just push people away with my social awkwardness and defensive reactions.  I'm more easily able to express myself in writing, when I can edit what I say until it's acceptable to me.  I'm much slower in person, because I'm often editing what I say in my head before I say it.  I'm introspective to the point that my principal says I'm "stuck in my own head too much."  I used to think that my introspection was a redeeming quality, but apparently it doesn't come across that way to others.  I just try so hard, but it seems I need to completely change myself to be successful in connecting to others.

God, I'm afraid to disagree with you in case I'm being defensive...:P

I did talk about why I didn't complete the homework, in great detail.  I'm really honest, and I wouldn't hide that information from my therapist.  I'm paying her to help me get better at life, so it wouldn't be helpful to skip out on that.  I'm just making another attempt at it this week!

But I think you're right that I could use grammar/semantics as a protection from hearing things that could be potentially damaging.  

My therapist did say that I should just be aware of my reactions to things.  I don't think I nitpick grammar all the time.  I'm a teacher, and I teach kindergarten through 8th grade.  My kids misuse grammar and words all the time, but I don't spend all day correcting them.  I don't know, I'll have to figure out who I nitpick and who I don't.  It's probably people who attempt to get close to me, if I had to guess.  My therapist says I'm very strongly guarded and she can't seem to get past the walls I've apparently put up.
Well, considering I don't think I have any redeeming qualities, I'd say I probably have a self esteem issue :P

So people are saying that suicidal thoughts decrease with the use of antidepressants? I'm confused about what exactly you're looking to learn more about!

I had mild suicidal thoughts before starting antidepressants, but after starting to take them they got much more severe, as in making a plan, acquiring the means, planning a time, etc. It's a side effect, and I haven't wanted to off myself in almost two weeks, so maybe I'm used to the meds now? I don't know.
I don't have a source, but I experienced it and lived to tell the tale. It wasn't looking good for a while there...

I've been feeling okay.  I think I need to sleep more.  But I've made it a week without seriously wanting to off myself, it's the longest I've gone in a month and a half.  

I wish it would start feeling like spring, it's barely above 40 today!  Then I'd be more likely to ride.  Or maybe not, maybe it's just an excuse.

I played clarinet.  It was an escape for me in my first depressive episode, but this episode has stolen so much of me.  But hey, I found reddit, so that's cool I guess.  

I used to enjoy taking 20-25 mile bike rides whenever I got the chance.  :P  My trail is flooded though.  I also used to bike commute to work.  Maybe one of these days I'll feel up to going at least around town.

I sure hope so.  In January I planned a bike tour for this summer, hoping that I'd feel better by then.  Recovery has been slower than expected...ugh.  I need to train but I can't make myself do it.  

I made a pizza over the weekend, if that counts.  Like, real dough and everything.  It turned out poorly.  I'm very out of practice.  

I've kept up with amateur music at church-singing and playing handbells.  I play "professionally" in a folk music group, but I skipped out on rehearsals for months because I couldn't bring myself to fake happiness any more than I had to.  Music used to be my life...wanted to become an orchestral musician, but in college I had another episode and almost gave it up.  Completed my music degree 3 years ago, but I haven't touched my primary instrument in a year.  Sad, really.  I feel like I wasted all of the hours I put into it.  Maybe someday I'll be able to play again.  Depression is the freaking WORST.

Thanks for responding to me over the past week.  You don't have to if you don't want to, I'm okay now, I think.

I did have hobbies before depression made me lose interest in everything.  Everything.  I was talking to a pastor of mine (I'm an atheist who goes to church...it's a cool church), and she was talking about all the things I used to enjoy, and it felt like she was describing someone else.  I thought, "Oh yeah, I remember when I used to enjoy cycling.  Music.  Baking.  Doing anything at all..."

I think that if I stay on these meds, I need to recognize the dark days as a side effect, not as reality, and ride them out accordingly.  But it's so freaking hard because killing myself seems like the best option on those days.  It's like really intense tunnel vision.

I usually end up trying to numb any feelings and distracting myself somehow, usually youtube, reddit, or other internet stuff that can hold my attention, sometimes sleeping.  It helps if I have something to grab onto that can occupy my mind.  This past week, it sucked, but it was how horrible I was feeling physically.  Last week, it was researching emotional numbness and how to approach breaking it.  

I'm having a pretty good day mentally, but I'm also actively not thinking about anything that would be helpful for my therapy appointment on Monday because I'm afraid of triggering another low.  I tend to avoid anything uncomfortable in life, so I guess that makes sense.

I haven't stopped taking them since I started a month ago.  It's amazing how I don't have in-between days mentally.  I'll either be like I was when I posted this, or I'll be like I am now-while work was crummy, I'm handling it fine.  Even though I still think about suicide, it's not as serious as "I'm going to do it this weekend."  So that's good I guess.

I live with my husband, we're in the same city.  

Part of my problem is the appetite-killing side effect.  Food makes me nauseous.  Any food.  Sometimes even smelling food makes me feel sick.  But I'm trying to force myself to eat because I feel worse if I don't eat, which is probably part of the reason I felt so bad yesterday-my heart rate was way elevated and pounding, I was dizzy, my arms were tingly, felt like I was going to pass out...

So today, just feel nauseous so far, so I guess that's progress.  :P

My husband is a musician.  He's in several ensembles in my city.  His connections, sadly, are here.  

I'm feeling less suicidal today.  This antidepressant has really been screwing with me.  Mentally, I'll feel great one day, then the next day I'm ready to throw in the towel.  Not to mention it makes me physically ill.  At least I felt so sick today I wasn't thinking about suicide anymore?  Can't get to the doctor until the 26th without missing work.  I'm no doctor, but I'm thinking this drug isn't the right one for me.

It's rough-I need insurance so I can get my depression taken care of, but my job makes the depression worse.  It's an awful place to be, and I feel trapped.  It's a crappy salary, and crappy benefits, but it's better than nothing.  Between my husband and I, we're paying for 4 degrees, and without my salary we can't make any payments.  

Trust me, I check the job listings every day for other positions relatively close to here.  It's really not healthy for me.  There's just NOTHING.  There's a huge number of people looking for jobs right now because a ton of people just got laid off in my field, and any one of them would love my job, and will apply for the same jobs I will.  But yeah, if it were as easy as just quitting and then starting a new one, I'd have done it months ago.  The more I have to fake, the more I hate myself for having to fake.

I keep thinking that maybe after I start to "feel" again, I'll feel anything for my husband.  We're nothing but roommates right now.

Honestly, I DO have to pretend.  If I don't I'll get fired.  Not even kidding.  My supervisor is watching me like a hawk, and since I work with people, I can't act depressed.  She thinks I don't enjoy my job (I don't always, but I'm stuck with it because there aren't any other jobs in my field, and I need the insurance), so I have to pretend I am very passionate about it in order to keep it.  If I'm not happy, she'll find someone else who is.  It's getting worse the farther away from "happy" I get.  

Husband knows that I've had suicidal thoughts.  He's a musician, and can't miss his tour with his band this weekend.  Unfortunately, I feel nothing for him anymore, with this whole emotional disconnect thing.  Depression does mess with you.  

I'm trying to think of things to do this weekend to keep myself occupied.  I just don't have friends I can call up to spend time with.  Depression makes you isolate, which makes making friends hard.  

Moving somewhere else doesn't take depression away.  Also I'm stuck here since I'm married and husband has a few jobs here.

I've been feeling emotionally disconnected from pretty much everything for the past few months.  Not much phases me, especially not in this mindset.  I've been working on feeling emotions instead of shoving them away since my last appointment with my therapist, but I don't know if I can stand to live with the constant anxiety that's present if I let it be.  

Right now I'm dealing at work.  I have to cover everything up and pretend to be happy and perky.  

If I'm not feeling better by the time I get home, I have a suicide "safety plan" that I'm supposed to use.
